part.text: [{"id":"R00629","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"Focuses on defending LLM applications against prompt injection and jailbreaking, not on using an LLM for an OS-level security task.","evidence":"The security of Large Language Model (LLM) applications is fundamentally challenged by \"formfirst\" attacks like prompt injection and jailbreaking"},{"id":"R00869","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"LLM assists Linux kernel patch migration, which is OS engineering without a stated security analysis, testing, or protection outcome.","evidence":"automating out-of-tree kernel patch migration"},{"id":"R03168","decision":"EXCLUDE","reason":"Uses a TEE to protect on-device LLMs; the LLM is the protected asset, not used for an OS security task.","evidence":"protecting on-device LLMs using Arm Trusted Execution Environment (TEE), TrustZone"},{"id":"R04909","decision":"POSSIBLE_CORE","reason":"LLM agent automates backporting of security patches to older branches, including for the Linux kernel.","evidence":"migrating mainline security patches to older branches"}]
